name: Sheraton Saigon Grand Opera Hotel
short_description: A full-service Sheraton at the junction of Dong Khoi and Dong Du streets in District 1, steps from the Saigon Opera House.
ai_summary: Sheraton Saigon Grand Opera Hotel occupies a corner site where Dong Khoi Street meets Dong Du Street in District 1, placing it within walking distance of the Saigon Opera House, Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica, and the Dong Khoi shopping strip -- from which the hotel took its updated name after a 2024 rebrand from Sheraton Saigon Hotel & Towers. Guest reviews are consistently strong on location, calling it hard to beat for reaching the city's landmark sights on foot, and repeatedly praise attentive, welcoming staff, a lively modern-decor atmosphere, and well-kept rooms and executive lounge. The hotel has followed up the naming refresh with a renovation of its Grand Opera Tower, addressing some of the age-related wear that older reviews mentioned. Recurring watchouts are more about cost and city noise than service quality: some guests find room rates and food pricey for the category, a few mention street noise reaching upper floors, and bathrooms in standard rooms run smaller than in some newer competitors. It suits travelers who want a central, full-service Sheraton within easy reach of District 1's main landmarks and shopping rather than the riverside stretch further east.

faqs.question: Is the Sheraton Saigon Grand Opera Hotel the same as the former Sheraton Saigon Hotel & Towers?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the property was officially renamed from Sheraton Saigon Hotel & Towers to Sheraton Saigon Grand Opera Hotel in 2024, a tribute to its proximity to the Saigon Opera House. The renaming came alongside a renovation of the Grand Opera Tower wing.

faqs.question: How far is Sheraton Saigon Grand Opera Hotel from Tan Son Nhat Airport?
faqs.answer: It's roughly 8 kilometers from Tan Son Nhat International Airport, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic, which can be significant in central Ho Chi Minh City at peak hours.
